mcqs.q: How was crime punished in Anglo-Saxon England?
options: Anglo-Saxons punished all crimes with imprisonment in castle dungeons.
The 1875 Act made the NHS free for all workers.
Anglo-Saxons had no laws and just took revenge on each other.
Through wergild ('man-price') compensation for victims, communal responsibility via tithings, trial by ordeal in disputed cases, and the death penalty for serious crimes.
Stalin took power by leading the Red Army to victory in the Civil War.
Stalin took power because Lenin nominated him as his successor.
No — Lenin's Testament (1922-23) warned against Stalin's rudeness and recommended his removal; Stalin won by manoeuvring against Trotsky after Lenin's death.
Anglo-Saxons punished all crimes with imprisonment in castle dungeons.

mcqs.q: Why did public health reforms accelerate after 1848?
options: The 1875 Act made the NHS free for all workers.
The 1848 Public Health Act followed cholera epidemics and Chadwick's report; John Snow's 1854 Broad Street pump study reinforced the case for clean water by 1875.
Stalin took power by leading the Red Army to victory in the Civil War.
Public health acts were passed because Victorians discovered germs in the 1840s.
